segments.text: Good evening. This is Aakashwani and I am Nishit Kumar with the news at nine.
The headlines
Durga Puja being celebrated with religious fervor in many parts of the country.
Home Minister Ramit Shah visits injured people in Kolkata's Pandal stampede
while seven accused send to 10 day police custody.
In France police arrests 1800 people after violent clashes and looting during nationwide
by demonstrations over rising living costs and poor school conditions.
Orange alert for very heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu, Pura Cherry and Karayk until Wednesday.
Asian Paraguams begin in Aichi Nagoya in Japan, over 150 athletes from India, to aim for
over 100 medals and in Squash India's location Shubramani wins the boys under 17
title at Malaysia jr. open and now the news in detail today is an additional day
of Mahasabthami the day is being celebrated with religious fervor in
many parts of the country in Odisha beautifully decorated pandals and
temples are drawing large numbers of devotees special rituals are being
performed at Shakti Pete's while major cities including Bhuvaneshwar and
Kathakar witnessing festive gatherings and elaborate decorations the
celebrations reflect Odisha's rich cultural heritage and the enduring
significance of Goddess Durga as the symbol of divine power and the triumph of good or evil.
We have a report.
The capital city of Bhubaneswar and the Silver City Katak are glowing with festive splendor
as elaborately decorated Durga Puja Pendles draw large crowds of visitors after sunset.
From magnificent temple-inspired gateways to artistic structures modeled on famous landmarks
across India and abroad, the Pendles showcase a remarkable blend of devotion, architecture
and creativity.
Colorful illuminations, intricate decorations, and beautifully adorned idols of Goddess Durga
have transformed the twin cities into vibrant festive destinations.
In Kataq, the traditional silver-filled decorations, popularly known as Chandi Mehta, are a distinctive
charm to the celebrations.
Devotees and visitors are making evening rounds of the pendels, enjoying the festive
atmosphere, food stalls, and cultural attractions.
Durgapuja celebrations have gripped Barak Valley of Assam with colourful eliminations
in elaborately decorated pandals attracting large crowds across Kachar, Sirbhoomi and
Hailakande.
The festivities highlight the region's rich Bengali cultural heritage and interfaith harmony
with members of Hindu and Muslim communities working together in pandal decorations
and crowd management.
Local authorities have put safety measures in place to ensure peaceful celebrations.
In Gujarat, the festival is celebrated as Navaratri, with utmost enthusiasm and religious
fervour.
All the cities across the state are celebrating the festival with massive Ras Garba events.
However, in West Bengal, after the Chorbhaggan stampede incident in Kolkata, the celebration
of Durga Puja has been toned down.
Our correspondent reports, Home Minister Amit Shah visited the injured in hospital
today.
We have a report.
The tragic Chorbhagan incident has cast a pall of gloom over Durga Puja celebrations in Kolkata.
On Mahasabh Tommy's footfall at several major puja pandals remained low,
with many committees cancelling cultural programs, community fests and other festive activities.
Loudspeakers and talk trunks have also fallen silent at several pandals.
The move follows Chief Minister Shubhinder Adhikar's apple to Puja organizers
to avoid extra-vagnous and restrict celebrations to religious rituals.
Meanwhile, security has been tightened at major pandals with increased surveillance at
entry and exit points, enhanced crowd management and more volunteers.
Coordination with the police has also been strengthened.
The chief minister today held a high-level meeting on Puja security at Bhavanibhavan and
later visited the state police control room to review the situation.
The administration has said that maximum vigilance is being maintained to ensure
the safety of visitors during the remaining days of Durga Puja.
In the wake of a tragic incident at Chorbhagan, Kolkata Police have imposed prohibitory orders
under section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagar Eksuraksha Sangita in a large area surrounding Chorbhagan,
including Central Avenue for the next three days.
In the meantime, court has ordered 10-day police custody to seven people,
arrested by Kolkata Police in connection with the stampede at the Chorbhagan-Sharbhajani-Durgot-Shabshavmiti-Durgapuja-Pandal.
Home Minister Amit Shah today visited the injured person at hospitals before going back to Delhi.
Shundi Pandash Gupta, Aghashpani News, Kolkata.
In Punjab, eight workers of Vixit Bharat G. Ramji including women have been killed and
several others injured when a four-wheeler rammed into them on Lehra Ga Ga Jackal Road in
Sanguru district this evening. The victims were reportedly working on the roadside
when the speeding car mowed them down. Sanguru Superintendent of Police,
Palvendar Singh Chima told media that injured have been shifted to various hospitals.
He said the vehicle has been identified and police would nap the driver soon.
Union Home Minister Mishra is visiting Punjab to share the pain of the Buri families whose
members have recently been killed for raising their voices against drugs traffickers in
the state.
He will be meeting the families of those who recently lost their lives in Mansa, Gurdaspur
and Sanguru districts after raising their voice against the Chitta that is synthetic
drug traffickers who have allegedly been flourishing under the patronage of the
AAP government. The Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations IFSO unit of
Delhi Police has prevented 1 crore, 53 lakh rupees cyber fraud across five
states. The unit tracks suspicious money trails and identified victims of the
cyber fraud through timely intervention in five cases across Delhi, Rajasthan,
Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Gujarat. Most of the cases relate to
elderly citizens targeted through digital arrest camps.
Delhi police has urged citizens to remember that there is no such thing as digital arrest
in law.
It has also asked the citizens to immediately call the National Cyber Crime Helpline 1930
or report at cybercrime.gov.in.
Maharashtra's first advanced Annapurati grain ATM was inaugurated by the state Food,
Civil Supplies and Consumer Protection Minister Chagan Bhojbal in Nashik.
The initiative aims to provide food grains to eligible beneficiaries at their convenience
beyond the fixed operating hours of fair price shops.
Maharashtra has around 54,000 fair price shops serving approximately 7-7.45 crore beneficiaries
under the public distribution system, PDS.
This is Aakashwani giving you the news.
Stay connected with AIR News, followers on X at AIR News Alerts and visit newsaunair.gov.in
for the latest updates.
Welcome back to the news at 9.
In France, police arrested at least 1800 people across the country after violent groups
clashed with officers and looted shops during nationwide demonstrations.
Hundreds of thousands of people took part in agitations denouncing rising living costs
and poor conditions in schools.
Authorities said mass groups set fire and attacked public buildings in several cities
yesterday.
In Limoges, a city in central France flames and gulf the 19th century city hall causing
its roof to collapse.
Paris police said in a statement one person died of a heart attack without providing further
details.
Interior Minister Lauren Nunez said more than 500 police officers,
gendarmes, and firefighters were injured. French President Emmanuel Macron is
holding an emergency meeting with top government officials. He will address
the nation later in the evening. Indian Embassy in Riyadh has advised the
Indian community in Saudi Arabia to take due precautions under the prevailing
situation and immediately proceed to the nearest safe place in case of
air rail attacks. In an advisory issue today, the embassy urged them to refrain from filming,
publishing or sharing any information, photos or videos related to the ongoing events.
The embassy officials continue to visit hospitals where injured Indian nationals
are receiving medical treatment and are in constant touch with their family and providing
necessary assistance. Meanwhile, Riyadh's international airport remains closed to flight
operations. Zamam, Jeddah and Medina airports remain operational, although some disruptions
continue. Indian carriers have extended the suspension of flights to and from Saudi Arabia.
The embassy said Saudi airlines continues to operate schedule flights to Indian destinations
from Dhammam, Jeddah and Medina. It asked international requiring urgent departure to
consider transiting via Bahrain, Kuwait or Qatar subject to obtaining the necessary
visas. Indian nationals planning to travel to Saudi Arabia including for Umrah have
been advised to take into account the ongoing disruptions at Saudi airports.
Ukrainian forces launched one of the largest aerial assaults on Russia today, sending more
than 1,000 drones across the country and setting ablaze an oil export terminal in St. Petersburg.
Russia's defence minister said its forces had destroyed over 1,000 Ukrainian drones
over 15 Russian regions as well as Russian-controlled Ukrainian peninsular Crimea and the Black
Sea.
The Russian forces launched two attacks on the southern Ukrainian city of Zaforizia, killing
a woman and injuring two.
Iran's newly appointed Defense Minister Mehdad Akhlaqi has warned US President Donald Trump
against launching further attacks on Iran, asserting that Tehran has taken all necessary
measures to counter the mother of all bombs and is confident in its military preparedness.
Akhlaqi's remarks came after Iran's parliament approved his appointment as Minister of
Defence and Armed Forces logistics today.
You are listening to the news at 9 on Akashwani.
Welcome back.
The India Meteorological Department, IMD, has issued an orange colour warning for heavy
to very heavy rainfall of Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karakal till the 21st of this month.
Heavy rainfall is also likely to prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Mahi, and South-intended
Karnataka during the next two to three days.
The Asian Paragames 2026 began today in Aichi, Nagoya, Japan, with India aiming to build on
its record medal hall at the previous edition.
The fifth edition of the continental sporting event will run until October 24, featuring
competitions across 18 spots.
thoughts. The opening ceremony was held at Paloma Mejuo Stadium in Nagoya. India is targeting
a 100-metal hole with Para Athletics head coach Satya Narayana expressing confidence in the
contingent's preparation, determination and ability to deliver a strong performance. Para
badminton player Pramod Bhagat and sprinter Simran Sharma leading the Indian contingent
as flag bearers. India has sent over 150 athletes to compete in 11 disciplines. The
event will be streamed live on the Wave's OTT app and Prasar Bharati Sports YouTube
channel.
India's Lokesh Subramani won the boys under 17 titles at the Malaysia Squash Junior Open
beating local challenger Muhammad Ifwat Zulkifli in straight games in the final in Kuala Lumpur
today.
Lokesh seeded second, defeated his opponent 11-6, 11-2, 11-8.
Adya Budhia and Aryaman Singh reached the semi-finals in the under-17 girls and boys categories.
In women's cricket, Zimbabwe have set a target of 103 runs for India in the second T20 international
of the three masteries at the Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh International Cricket Stadium
in Raipur.
In reply, India were 62 for no loss in 5.2 overs when reports last came in.
Opting to bat first, Zimbabwe scored 102 for 8 in their allotted 20 overs.
led by Smriti Mandana. India lead the three-match series 1-0 after securing a
four-wicket victory in the opening match at the same venue on Friday. In a special
initiative, female spectators have been allowed free entry to all the three
T20 internationals following a suggestion by Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu
Deusai. The third and the final T20 international will be played on the
20th of this month. The Indian Navy's three musted sale training ship INS
So, Darshani has departed Sallala in Oman, continuing her historic trans-oceanic deployment
Lokhayan, 2026.
The ship visited Oman from 14th to 17th of this month.
The Defence Minister said that during the port call, professional interactions and
sporting engagements fostered camaraderie and reinforced bonds of friendship between
the Indian Navy and the Royal Navy of Oman.
Minister of Housing Affairs Manohar Lal has said that Namo-Bharat Rapid Rail is
ushering in a new era of regional connectivity in India. He said this while addressing the
Namo Bharat Divas 2026, which was celebrated to mark three successful years of its operations.
He noted that the 82-kilometer-long Delhi-Ghaziabad-Mirat corridor has recorded
over 4.5 crore passengers' journeys. And now, before we end the bulletin, the headlines once again.
Durga Puja being celebrated with religious fervor in many parts of the country.
Home Minister Amit Shah visits injured people in Kolkata's Pandal stampede, while seven
accused send to 10-day police custody.
In France, police arrest 1,800 people after violent clashes and looting during nationwide
demonstrations over rising living costs and poor school conditions.

Wednesday.
